title: ADV-050: QA study and independent reproduction
scope: Five English chapters. Each opening excerpt is a self-contained short-form clip. Remaining narration expands it. Examples are synthetic or bounded software controls.

en.title: What a test can show
en.clip_text: A green test suite is not enough to claim that a model works. This study evaluates a QA instrument, not a new theory. Before testing, we fix the domain, units, tolerance, invariants, and an independent oracle. Then we run a baseline and specific mutations, such as reversing a sign or doubling a coefficient. The question is whether tests detect deliberate changes. Each result stays linked to its parameters, code, and artifacts for later review. This separates model correctness from test sensitivity.
en.long_extra: If the program and oracle share a formula and integrator, they can share an error. So the suite compares distinct implementations at multiple observations. The contract defines success before results are known. A failing baseline blocks interpretation of its mutants; a small variation may survive if it falls below tolerance. The threshold is not changed afterward. The package preserves hashes and outputs so reviewers can trace each classification. We distinguish synthetic calculations, kernel controls, and earlier campaigns. I’m Cristian Guerra, known as criguex, a Colombian QA Automation professional from Medellín, with more than eight years of experience. I authored this QA study and independent reproduction through contributions to strategy, mutations, resources, and validation. AI tools are disclosed as assistance for analysis and code preparation, not as coauthors or co-discoverers. OpenAI is credited for the original proofs; this study does not claim authorship of them or discovery of a theorem. The contribution is making tests, detected failures, and limits auditable.

en.title: Nine synthetic models
en.clip_text: The suite contains nine synthetic models: an RC circuit, Newton cooling, second-order consumption, Beer–Lambert attenuation, Snell refraction, a thin lens, an acoustic interface, an illustrative Fechner scale, and a synthetic logistic response. One concrete example is the RC circuit. With one kiloohm and one millifarad, its nominal time constant is one second. Deliberately changing tau changes the recorded output. These are reproducible calculations, not laboratory measurements. Each model has three nondegenerate configurations in the fixed contract, with units and observations specified.
en.long_extra: The RC case runs for three seconds, with sixty-four, one hundred twenty-eight, and two hundred fifty-six integration steps. At three seconds and the finest resolution, the baseline records 4.751 volts; doubling tau records 3.884. These are rounded JSON values, not physical readings. The nominal time constant is resistance multiplied by capacitance: tau equals R times C. Other oracles are distinct: closed-form solutions for several ODEs, bisection for Snell, ray tracing for the lens, a boundary system for acoustics, and numerical integration for Fechner. The logistic model is a synthetic response to normalized stimulus, between zero and one; Fechner is illustrative, not a universal law. Some configurations share mathematical structure after rescaling, so nine names do not mean nine independent regimes. No experimental measurements were used. Plots retain units and calculated points. The suite examines detection of known changes in controlled examples; it does not certify real-world performance.

en.title: Narrow formal controls
en.clip_text: The kernel control uses a minimal fixture: target states zero equals zero and is proved with rfl. The mutation keeps the declared type but replaces the proof value with a proof of True. Lean and nanoda accept the baseline and reject that incompatible value. This is a typechecking control for one declaration, contrasting the declared type with the exported proof value. Separately, Lean accepts a nonzero constant field in periodic Navier–Stokes, with zero pressure and force and unit viscosity. These controls have distinct scopes.
en.long_extra: Lean reports that True does not match the expected type; nanoda reaches a definitional-equality assertion. This pair is a bounded control. The periodic example is on a torus, and its axiom report lists three axioms: propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. A constant velocity does not have finite energy over all of R³, so it does not transfer to the Euclidean problem. After the clean-source build, Comparator independently rechecked the Navier–Stokes and Euler challenges with both nanoda and Lean. Calibration included two positive fixtures accepted and four negative fixtures rejected before kernel calls. These recorded results are not universal verification. Exact names appear on screen, and preserved artifacts let reviewers inspect the harness, declarations, and outputs without changing original theorem sources.

en.title: Paired campaign results
en.clip_text: The suite ran on macOS arm64 and Linux x86_64. Each environment evaluated the same eighty-four variants: twenty-seven baseline PASS, fifty-four mutant KILLED, and three tiny calibration SURVIVED. Classifications and parameters match across hosts. These are paired runs of one suite, not one hundred sixty-eight distinct cases. Survivors remain in the report without forcing rejection. Counts are per host, with explicit denominators; another platform added no cases. This distinction matters when reporting totals and comparing results across both hosts side by side.
en.long_extra: The comparison included seven hundred thirty-eight finite values and eighteen non-finite outputs from the chemical sign-reversal mutant, represented as null. The largest normalized difference between finite values was about 1.11 times ten to the minus sixteen. Each baseline uses an independent oracle and normalized error tolerance of 10⁻⁶ against a fixed scale. ODEs use their last applicable resolution; algebraic models receive no invented refinements. In fifteen ODE baselines, error decreased with refinement and observed orders were near four; this is diagnostic, not a general bound. The largest fine ODE error was about 1.12 times ten to the minus nine in a logistic case. Fechner reached about 7.63 times ten to the minus eight with a trapezoidal oracle. Tiny RC mutations survive under this contract; that does not establish equivalence. The campaign tests detection of known changes and cross-platform consistency. JSON and classifications were preserved when CSV export was corrected.

en.title: Reproducibility and limits
en.clip_text: The review package links code, records, and reproducible checks. Public release follows author approval. Reproducing files is not repeating experiments. The useful result is a traceable path from contract to data. This helps audit decisions, catch export mistakes, and preserve criteria fixed before execution. Earlier campaigns are documented separately, with parameters and results preserved for review.
en.long_extra: Local verification confirmed artifact integrity, CSV rows, and cross-host correspondence. Clean03 completed the source build with exit code zero and 11,424 jobs; it reused dependencies and toolchain cache, so it was not a full bootstrap. After that build, Comparator rechecked the Navier–Stokes and Euler challenges with both nanoda and Lean. Earlier ODE context is separate from this suite: one hundred fifty recorded runs in groups of ninety, thirty, and thirty, not one hundred fifty independent cases. Maximum errors were about 1.30 times ten to the minus five at step 0.05; 7.24 times ten to the minus seven at 0.025; and 4.27 times ten to the minus eight at 0.0125, against fine tolerance 10⁻⁶. Taylor–Green V1 illustrates flow; it is not a formal construction or evidence of blow-up. The contribution is contracts, failures detected by known mutations, repetition across two environments, and traceable evidence. Cristian Guerra, criguex, QA Automation, receives credit for the QA study and independent reproduction; AI is listed as assistance. OpenAI is credited for the original proofs. No new theorem or validation of an open mathematical problem is claimed. We invite review of scope, data, and limitations before reuse.
